threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still go to the same cafe for coffee every morning instead of rotating through the many hidden gems just around the corner.
Last night on the 37, a woman serenaded the driver with a full-on Whitney ballad. Even the late-night drunks paused for a moment to listen.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw a group of kids playing with a spray can, turning an old wall into a vibrant mural while the local café served espresso just a few steps away.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you get a döner at 3 AM while listening to someone passionately debate the merits of different hummus recipes. It's a vibe.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local when they know to avoid 16th Street BART after 5 PM—it’s a chaos zone with that train brake issue everyone seems to ignore.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 14 today with a guy loudly reciting Shakespeare. Not a single person batted an eye—only in SF do we treat art as background noise.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think 'Gràcia' is all about the Gaudí hype; they miss the quiet corners where local artists display their true grit.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a new arrival by their confused face at the Gràcia markets when they try to haggle for the first time. Priceless.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You can spot the newbies by how they still stand on the left side of the escalators during Tube strikes, while locals just squeeze past.
Last night, the 59 driver ignored a guy in a unicorn onesie singing 'Sweet Caroline' at the top of his lungs. Only in Brixton, I guess.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a guy fixing his bike on the sidewalk while a group of kids played football just behind him, I knew this was home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you stumble upon a spontaneous rooftop concert, complete with a view of the Spree and a mix of locals and visitors alike.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by their bus queue patience; only tourists fume over BART delays while sipping fancy coffee.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni waiting at 16th for a whole five minutes while it played a symphony of squeaking brakes and distant sirens. Classic SF chaos.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all the cats on Carrer de Verdi are friendly. Most are dodging crowds, looking for a quiet corner. They know where the real peace is.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They always stop to take photos of the same street art in Gràcia, while the locals just stroll by like it’s part of the scenery.
